title: AI, Ethics, and Society
description: How AI reshapes rights, institutions, work, the environment and public life, and how to make defensible decisions about building, buying and deploying it.
stagesNote: The course starts with ethical frameworks, then applies them to harms to individuals, to effects on society, and finally to the institutions that govern AI.

text.lessons: The full text of each lesson, grouped by week. The course assigns the lessons that are not marked Optional; the optional lessons are further reading and case studies. Labs are marked, and a tag such as A2 links to the assessment a lesson supports.
text.slides: Slide decks for the lessons, as they are posted. Use the arrow keys to move through a deck, press F for full screen, and press Esc to come back to this page.
text.resources: Frameworks, standards, incident trackers and media used across the course. The Lessons column shows where each one comes up.
text.assessments: The six graded components of the course, with what each asks for, when it is due, and how it is graded.
